answer: A ledge admits one climber, so scaling must pay for space. Each identity needs two holders outside its own face to vouch at a ledge, and one vouch serves one identity, so n aliases need n distinct vouchers rather than a single ring. Every ledge is priced by rank: the k-th vouch an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed. Standing climbs toward the zenith tier only while audits re-walk each vouch; an unconfirmed vouch clears the ledge and forfeits its bonds. Each orchard plot backs one identity and cannot be pooled or resold.
